# Extra analysis tables v2 (generated by analysis/extra_analysis.py; headline = deterministic re-scoring, D11; stratification corrected, D13)

**Scope and uncertainty.** Intervals condition on the collected sessions: they cover item sampling only and exclude judge, scoring, contamination and restart-to-restart uncertainty. The same-arm repeats (A1/A2, B1/B2) agree to 0-2 items per benchmark and are identical on all 200 Layer 2 prompts, which is observed repeatability on these prompts, not proof that session uncertainty is negligible in general. Scope: this server, image, overlay revision, greedy decoding.

Direction: **B is slower than A on prose and faster than A on code** in these isolated decode benchmarks. The ratios are of arm medians (B/A); a ratio above 1 means B is faster. The code ratio of about 1.4 comes from one fixed benchmark prompt (one prompt per condition); why the stock arm decodes that prompt more slowly was not investigated (a difference in speculative-draft acceptance on that prompt is one candidate, unverified). In the mixed 4-stream harness workload (table below) per-request tok/s differs by only a few percent between arms, so the isolated code advantage should not be read as a general speed gain, and the prose slowdown should not be read as general either. All H3 intervals are narrow because the three medians within a session are nearly identical (session-to-session spread is not captured, see sensitivity).

The D2 statement that this interval mostly shows session-to-session spread is **not supported**: the six values per arm are three batch medians within each of two sessions, so the interval reflects within-session repetition; two sessions per arm cannot characterise restart variability. The pooling of dependent observations is a limitation of the pre-registered construction. The clean-only column drops A1's first decode median (taken during the full benchmark run in which the A1 speed-step contaminated poll occurred, see D8 section) and is the protocol-compliant check for the zero-contamination speed rule.

### D8 sensitivity (a): session x step x attempt poll counts
Columns: 'original rule' = running + waiting - harness_in_flight > 0 (PROTOCOL 2); 'D8 rule' = running > in_flight or (waiting > 0 and running >= 5); 'speed/layer1 rule' = waiting > 0 or running > 5, the stricter step-specific rule that governs those two steps under both versions (it is NOT the protocol's original rule; the original rule is shown for every step in its own column). Polls missing `harness_inflight` are counted as 0 in-flight (errs toward flagging) and listed as: none. A1 ran on the PC harness (one attempt per step, no driver attempt log). Start ordinal = the n-th driver start of that step (restarts repeat the driver's attempt/rerun numbers); 'result' = the attempt that supplies the stored data (last).

A1 contaminated speed poll(s) (minutes counted from the start of the A1 speed step; clock times are not published): [{'minute_in_speed_step': 5.0, 'running': 5, 'waiting': 4, 'harness_inflight': 0}]. Timeline on the same time base: `bench.py` ended at ~2.2 and the full `bench_streams` run at ~17.8, so the poll at minute 5.0 falls inside the full `bench_streams` run (running 5, waiting 4, harness in-flight 0, which is also how the speed step normally looks because the harness does not count the benchmark tool's own requests). Whether the 9 concurrent requests were the tool's own stage transition or foreign traffic cannot be resolved from telemetry; the conservative handling is the clean-only column in the H3 table (A1's first decode median dropped). The decode repetitions 2 and 3 are separate runs with no flagged polls.
